requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
The implementation covers every obligation. One boundary of the opening-fence rule has no test, so I judge the requirement not fully verified.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Opening fence of at least three colons, immediately followed by `{req} <name>`:** `colon_fence` (src/lib.rs:803) requires at least 3 colons. `definition_blocks` (src/lib.rs:649) then strips the `{req}` prefix straight off the text after the colons and requires whitespace before a valid name.
- **Closing fence has at least as many colons as the opening fence, with nothing else on the line but whitespace:** the `close_index` search in `definition_blocks` checks `count >= fence_length && suffix.trim().is_empty()`. `closes` in src/fenced.rs does the same for reference fences.
- **Indent of up to three spaces allowed; four or more is not a fence:** `colon_fence` rejects a line with more than 3 leading spaces. This applies to both opening and closing fences.
- **Body is all Markdown between the fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams and blank lines:** the body runs from the end of the opening line to the start of the closing line. Fence lines inside code blocks are skipped through `overlaps_protected`. `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs:413) builds the text through `without_options`.
- **No text after the closing fence:** the body ends at `body_end`, the start of the closing line.
- **Leading and trailing whitespace excluded in comparison:** `collect_definitions` calls `.trim()` on the text.

**Tests that exist**
- `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` (src/lib.rs:1597) covers three-space indent on open and close, a four-space indented opening fence, a four-space indented closing fence, trailing text on a closing line, trailing whitespace, and `{req}ready`.
- `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` (src/lib.rs:1581) covers a closing fence with fewer colons than the opening fence.
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` (src/evidence.rs:2982) covers headings, code blocks containing `:::`, and exclusion of text after the closing fence.
- `requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace` (src/evidence.rs:2885) covers whitespace trimming.
- `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` (src/evidence.rs:3015) covers a missing closing fence.
- `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` (src/evidence.rs:2255) covers a body that contains a `{req}` reference inside a code block.

**Gap**
The text says the opening fence needs "at least three colons", and `colon_fence` enforces that with `length >= 3`. No test checks that an opening fence with fewer than three colons, such as `::{req} x`, is not treated as a definition. My ripgreps over src/ and the project found no test with such a fence. Nothing checks either that whitespace between the colons and `{req}` stops the line being an opening fence. This is a named boundary of an obligation, it is conditional code, and the exemptions in step 5 do not apply. No `{fixme}` acknowledges it.
